note: v1 99.21 (seeds 0/11 99.21/99.20), The Kettle Modulates: Canterbury-ish prog at 126 bpm. A tune that never repeats a bar because its chord moves a third every bar (up a major third, down a minor), wurli and flute in unison; a 7/8 overture, a 5/8+6/8 verse where the flute sings over the contrary bass, a fuzz-organ solo over a 13/8 riff (3+3+3+2+2), a quiet 4/4 hymn with the tune in augmentation on the horn, a 7/8 recap a major third up that first wears the overture's clothes and then adds organ and horn, a held Fmaj9 to close. Draft 83 -> 99: the recap made to read as a return, dotted-eighth hats across the meters, a quiet hymn, EQ to the envelope.

v2 99.23 (seeds 0/11 99.23/99.22 vs v1 99.21/99.20): the fuzz solo gets an ARC. Twice (bars 8 and 16) the flute steps in and answers the organ with a bar of the kettle tune re-voiced on the riff's chord, a call and response; then for the last 8 bars the answers stop and the organ doubles itself an octave down, so the solo thickens into the hymn's hush. Answers every fourth bar split the section into too many short ones (recurrence 100 -> 87-92, 97.5-98.2), so two answers it is.

v3 99.25 (seeds 0/11 99.25/99.24 vs v2 99.23/99.22): a COUNTER-LINE in the verse and a blooming last chord. In the verse's second half the horn plays a guide-tone line: the 3rd or the 7th of each chord, whichever is nearest its last note, held for the bar and swelling, so a slow line creeps by the smallest steps (C Bb Ab B A C Bb Db B D C Eb) under the flute while the chords leap by thirds. In the coda, the flute trills between the 9th and the root over the held Fmaj9 instead of one held note.

v4 99.32 (seeds 0/11 99.32/99.31 vs v3 99.25/99.24): a new section, THE KETTLE - an 8-bar music-box interlude in 9/8 (2+2+2+3, a meter the song hadn't used) between the verse and the fuzz. The tune plays on a music box, a celesta follows it in canon a bar later and a fourth lower, and a clarinet holds root and fifth under them; in the last bar the flute whistles a chromatic run up an octave and a half over a snare crescendo, the kettle boiling over into the fuzz-organ section. It gives the title its moment and the song a breath before the loudest part.

v5 99.33 (seeds 0/11 99.33/99.31 vs v4 99.32/99.31): THE DOOR. The hymn's last two bars turn to C minor (Cm9, Fm7), and the horn, which has been singing the kettle tune in augmentation, quotes t1 Doors at Seven's SEVEN DOORS head cell in its own key (C5. Bb4 G4 F4 | Eb4 F4~). The Kettle Modulates joins t4 and t10 in answering the opener, at the quietest moment of the song, just before the recap's key change. Tried and dropped: the verse's guide-tone line returning high in the flute through the hymn blurred the hymn into the verse (seed 0 recurrence 100 -> 93, 98.41).
